title: ANDS Studio — AI-assisted drafting
walkthrough:
You are inside a dossier section's work panel. An eyebrow reads "Module … · Section … ·" with an applicability badge, and — when the leaf is placed — "· Placed at … · leaf …". Below sit the section title, a one-line purpose, and a "What Health Canada needs here" box with the guidance. Collapsed "Format & source" and (once the leaf exists) "eCTD placement" disclosures — the latter tagged with the lifecycle operation — sit behind their own expanders.

An action bar labelled "Choose how to complete this section" holds toggle buttons with icons: "Upload", "Author in-app", and "Mark N/A". Choosing "Author in-app" on an AI-enabled section reveals a second toggle: "💬 Draft with AI" (default) and "Fill the form".

In "Draft with AI" a bordered note headed by a green shield reads "How this AI draft is controlled", listing four bold lines: the draft is "Not filable on its own"; "You sign off, by name"; "Provenance is recorded"; and "Modeled on HC criteria — not HC's eValidator" — the structural completeness check is a technical checker, not Health Canada's official eValidator, with a muted "(Criteria last verified against HC guidance …)" date. A "More on how the AI is kept accountable" expander holds further reassurance. A grey line repeats that the assistant asks for details it needs and that nothing is saved until you click "Use this draft".

An empty thread shows "Tell it about the submission to get started — it knows what [section title] needs." You type into a two-row box (placeholder "e.g. Sponsor is Acme Pharma Inc., contact regulatory@acme.example") and press "Send"; Enter also sends. The button reads "Thinking…" while the reply streams in as chat bubbles.

Once a reply finishes, a "Use this draft →" button appears ("Saving…" while it works). A saved-document card shows a 💬 icon, the filename, size, a "fingerprint md5 …" label with the checksum's first eight characters, a provenance chip, and a "Download" link. Hovering the chip explains the draft was made under your direction, recorded in the audit trail, sent to the configured provider for this draft only (isolated per sponsor, never shared or used for training), and must be reviewed and confirmed before filing.

Above the card sits a red banner with a warning triangle: "Not yet filable — review required. This is an AI-assisted draft. It will not count as complete and the submission cannot be exported until you review it against the Health Canada guidance and attest it as your own content:" followed by a button "I have reviewed this AI draft — it is my content" ("Recording…" while saving). Until you click it the chip reads "AI draft — review & confirm". Once confirmed, it reads "AI-assisted · confirmed".

If the AI backend isn't configured, the chat shows a note that AI drafting isn't turned on yet, that you can author by hand since the form fills the same eCTD leaf, and to contact your administrator — with a "Fill the form instead →" button.

The alternate "Fill the form" tab authors the same leaf from a template form. Fields marked "example — replace this" show greyed placeholder text; a warning names any field still carrying the example and states the section stays "not filable" until replaced. Its "Review vs Health Canada" action returns findings. Either path saves an unconfirmed draft the review banner blocks until you confirm.
